chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Amr ibn al-Miqdam, from his father, from Salama ibn Kuhayl, who said:

I heard Ali (peace be upon him) saying to Shurayh: 'O Shurayh, look to those who delay payment and those who withhold the rights of people, from those with means and wealth, who pledge the wealth of Muslims to the rulers. So take the rights of the people from them, and sell their real estate and houses in order to satisfy those rights, for I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saying: "The delay of payment by a wealthy Muslim is oppression against the Muslims."'
And whoever has no real estate, nor a house, nor wealth, there is no recourse against him.
And know that it is not those who compel people to the truth, but rather those who restrain them from falsehood.
Then be even-handed among the Muslims in your face, speech, and sitting place, so that your close one does not hope for your partiality, and your enemy does not despair of your justice.
And return the oath to the claimant along with his evidence, for that is clearer for removing confusion and more established for the judgment.

And know that Muslims are trustworthy (accepted as witnesses) one towards another, except one who has been flogged for a fixed punishment and has not repented from it, or is known for false testimony, or is a person of slight credibility.
And beware of showing irritation in the court of judgment, in which Allah has mandated reward and enriches for the one who judges with the truth.
And know that settlement (conciliation) is permissible among Muslims, except a settlement that makes halal what is haram, or makes haram what is halal.
And set a time limit for one who claims absent witnesses between them; if he brings them forward, you take his right for him, and if he does not bring them forward, you impose the case (against him).

And beware of executing a judgment in retribution (qisas) or a fixed punishment (hadd) from the punishments of Allah, or a right from the rights of Muslims, until you present that to me, if Allah wills.
And do not sit in the court of judgment until you eat.
ai.seo_question: What are the key judicial guidelines given by Imam Ali to Shurayh regarding debt collection, witness credibility, and court etiquette?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, serves as a foundational manual for Shia jurisprudence, detailing the ethical and procedural standards for Qadis (judges) under Imam Ali’s direct supervision. It highlights the practical application of debt collection from the wealthy (*al-musir*) and establishes the criteria for witness credibility, while emphasizing that conciliation (*sulh*) is valid unless it contravenes divine law. The instruction to refer major judgments to the Imam underscores the hierarchical nature of early Shia judicial authority and the importance of maintaining impartiality to prevent bias from relatives or enemies.
